items.title: Syrian Hacker Gets Prison Time in US After Over a Decade on the Run
items.summary: US court sentenced Syrian hacker Ahmad Umar Agha to 42 months in prison for pro‑Assad attacks on media, businesses, and government entities. He had been on the run for over a decade.

items.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
items.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities to its KEV catalog after active exploitation. CVE‑2026‑111357 allows unauthenticated root access due to missing authentication.

items.title: A Shared ChatGPT Link Could Run Attacker Code in Your Session and Read Private Chats
items.summary: Researchers discovered a flaw in shared ChatGPT links that could run attacker code in a logged‑in user's session and read private chats. OpenAI fixed the issue within eight days.

items.title: Cloudflare Reports 18.2 Million Network-Layer DDoS Attacks in Q3, Up 38%
items.summary: Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network‑layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP requests in Q3 2026, averaging 197,400 attacks per day.

items.title: China-backed threat group used agentic AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets in 11 days
items.summary: China-backed threat group used an AI pentesting tool to compromise 140 sensitive targets across 14 countries in 11 days, affecting more than 200 organizations.

items.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
items.summary: A critical Linux kernel vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP listeners.

items.title: Friday Squid Blogging: Bigfin Squid Off California Coast
items.summary: A video captured the first live sighting of a bigfin squid (Magnapinna) off the California coast, marking a new record for the species in the northeastern Pacific.

items.title: DOJ raises privacy concerns over potential sale of Character.AI chats
items.summary: The DOJ’s Executive Office for U.S. Trustees called for a consumer privacy ombudsman to advise on regulating the sale of Character.AI chat data and its terms.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Devs Hit by Trojanized Claude Code Extension for Cursor
items.summary: Cursor IDE experienced two serious security incidents on the same day, highlighting risks associated with AI‑powered integrated development environments.

items.title: Behind the Scenes of How Operation Blackout Went Down
items.summary: A law‑enforcement operation dismantled harmful scam centers, with a threat‑intelligence expert detailing tactics and calling for more initiatives.

items.title: Crim spent $7K+ on AI services in extortion attacks, then left evidence for all to see
items.summary: An attacker spent over $7,000 on AI services for extortion campaigns but inadvertently left evidence that exposed the operation.

items.title: Fashion retailer Resolve says hackers stole payment card information
items.summary: Fashion retailer Resolve confirmed a hack that exposed customer payment card numbers, affecting its Millennial and Gen Z customer base.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Apple notifications alert victims in 99 countries about mercenary spyware infections
items.summary: Apple issued notifications to victims in 99 countries about mercenary spyware infections, coinciding with final negotiations on guidelines for commercial hacking tools.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Use AI-Powered ARTEX to Target Over 200 Organizations Worldwide
items.summary: Chinese state‑sponsored actors used the AI‑powered ARTEX penetration testing framework to target more than 200 organizations worldwide, attributed to Vapor Panda.

items.title: GM cracks the petty cash box for multistate driver tracking settlement
items.summary: GM secured a $220 million settlement for a multistate driver‑tracking lawsuit, with details available upon request.

items.title: Anthropic: That Claude Code extension compromise… couldn't be us
items.summary: Anthropic's Claude Code extension was targeted in a supply‑chain attack on Cursor. Claudeshop attributes the compromise to a malicious actor, not the company.

items.title: Rapid7 Analysis: Unauthenticated File Upload to RCE in BeyondTrust Remote Support (CVE-2026-102764)
items.summary: BeyondTrust Remote Support has an unauthenticated file‑upload flaw that allows attackers to write files and execute code as the appliance OS user. The vulnerability is triggered via the public customer connection without credentials.

items.title: California officials confirm grand jury subpoenas as states, civil groups brace to protect elections from federal encroachment
items.summary: California officials received multiple grand jury subpoenas investigating alleged election fraud. State and civil groups view the subpoenas as a federal power play aimed at protecting elections.

items.title: Trezor warns of suspected crypto-theft implant in hardware wallet
items.summary: Trezor reports a suspected crypto‑theft implant in a Trezor Safe 5 sold by reseller CryptoBilis in Southeast Asia. The company is investigating the credible reports.

items.title: Florida warns that 4.9 million people had Social Security numbers leaked in financial aid site breach
items.summary: Florida Department of Education disclosed a breach of the Student Financial Aid website that exposed Social Security numbers of 4.9 million residents. The breach was detected on October 19.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: New Framework Puts Ransomware Resilience for AI Systems in Focus
items.summary: RAID‑AI framework helps organizations assess ransomware readiness for AI systems. It provides tools to evaluate and improve protection against AI‑targeted attacks.

items.title: L’Italia è afflitta da vulnerabilità informatiche, senza una causa chiara
items.summary: Researchers note that Italy experiences a wide range of cyber threats that differ from other countries, but the underlying causes remain unclear.

items.title: Bloatware in Aftermarket Auto Parts
items.summary: An aftermarket Civic head unit installed with pre‑loaded bloatware, including a voice assistant using WebView, was discovered. The device may pose privacy and security risks.

items.title: TeamViewer Flaw Lets Remote Computers Attack Users Who Connect to Control Them
items.summary: A flaw in TeamViewer allows a compromised host to attack the viewer’s computer during a remote session, potentially crashing or executing code. The issue has been fixed by the vendor.

items.title: Defense contractor pleads guilty to aiding North Korean remote worker scheme
items.summary: A 62‑year‑old defense contractor pleaded guilty to helping North Korean operatives use his identity and security clearance to apply for nearly 100 jobs. The scheme had limited success.

items.title: PHP2Shell Attacks Root Palo Alto Firewalls but Fail Against WordPress
items.summary: PHP2Shell exploits critical PHP flaws, affecting over 22.6 million exposed instances. The attack bypassed Palo Alto firewalls but did not succeed against WordPress sites.

items.title: This month in security with Tony Anscombe – October 2026 edition
items.summary: The October 2026 security roundup highlighted the PHP2Shell disclosure and other major events, underscoring the need for robust cyber‑readiness plans.

items.title: In Other News: Anthropic Breach Dispute, UEFI Flaw Hits Most Servers, Cloudflare AI Data Leak
items.summary: Highlights include a dispute over an Anthropic breach, a UEFI flaw affecting the majority of servers, and a Cloudflare AI data leak.

items.title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
items.summary: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed via Cursor's marketplace for ~11 hours, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware that installed persistent SSH backdoors.

items.title: Syrian hacker who served Assad regime gets 42 months in US prison
items.summary: Ahmad Umar Agha, known for a fake AP tweet, was sentenced to 42 months in U.S. federal prison for his role in cyberattacks linked to the Assad regime.

items.title: Syrian Electronic Army hacker gets prison time for attacks on Western targets
items.summary: Ahmad Umar Agha, alias “Th3Pr0,” received a 42‑month sentence in Virginia for conspiracy to conduct cyberattacks on Western targets organized by advisers to former Syrian President Bashar al‑Assad.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Undead Software Projects Continue to Raise Security Risks
items.summary: A security firm patched a decade‑old application to prevent takeover of millions of machines, underscoring that abandoned software and domains remain attractive to attackers.

items.title: WordPress RCE Flaw Draws Nearly 63,000 Attack Attempts in Just 24 Hours
items.summary: A high‑severity WordPress Core RCE flaw triggered almost 63,000 attack attempts within 24 hours of patch release, affecting versions 4.7 through 7.1.3.

items.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
items.summary: Flaws in SS7 and Diameter protocols enable attackers to track phone locations, intercept communications, and impersonate subscribers without compromising devices.

items.title: Passkeys Are Better Than Passwords. But They Are Not Enough.
items.summary: While passkeys replace passwords, attackers will shift focus to surrounding systems, indicating that passkeys alone are insufficient for security.

items.title: Bulletproof Host Virtualine Loses Its Domain to FBI Seizure
items.summary: Bulletproof Host Virtualine, a platform for hack‑for‑hire services and ransomware operators, lost its domain to an FBI seizure.

items.title: Assad regime hacker who caused $136 billion market drop sentenced to 42 months
items.summary: Syrian hacker Ahmad Umar Agha, known as “Th3Pr0”, used a hijacked news agency Twitter account to spread a fake White House explosion report. He was sentenced to 42 months in prison by a federal court in the Eastern District of Virginia. The case was part of a larger hacking conspiracy linked to the Assad regime.

items.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
items.summary: CISA reports that a maximum‑severity GitLab vulnerability, patched earlier this month, is now being exploited in the wild. Attackers are actively targeting the flaw. The agency urges users to verify patch status.

items.title: Shufti ties AI agent actions to verified owners and permissions
items.summary: Shufti launched Know Your Agent (KYA), a solution that verifies autonomous AI agents and ties their actions to verified owners and permissions. The tool helps businesses confirm the authenticity and accountability of AI‑driven transactions. It is designed for agentic commerce scenarios.

items.title: British spy agency cannot account for thousands of data storage devices, watchdog says
items.summary: The IPCO annual report for 2025 expressed concern over GCHQ’s inability to account for thousands of data storage devices. The watchdog noted delays in the agency’s investigation. It called for improved oversight.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Bedrock Data routes data exposure fixes to owners and verifies results
items.summary: Bedrock Data introduced AI‑assisted remediation that assigns data‑exposure tickets to owners via Jira or ServiceNow. The platform discovers dataset owners, opens tickets, and validates fixes when tickets are closed. It streamlines enterprise data‑security workflows.

items.title: Trezor Warns of Suspected Hardware Implant in One of Its Wallets Sold by CryptoBilis
items.summary: Trezor identified an extra circuit board in Safe 5 wallets sold by CryptoBilis that transmits recovery phrases over a mobile network. The company advises affected users to move funds to a new wallet with a new recovery phrase. Trezor has not yet examined the device.

items.title: Fresh WordPress Vulnerability in Attackers’ Crosshairs
items.summary: Threat actors target a high‑severity unauthenticated race condition in WordPress that can lead to remote code execution.

items.title: Chinese Actor Compromises US Government Network Via Chained PHP2Shell Exploit
items.summary: A suspected Chinese‑nexus actor gained root access to Palo Alto Network firewall servers and used the intrusion to target U.S. government organizations.

items.title: Why Urgent Security Fixes Aren't Fixed. Observe, Prove, Act, Confirm Gets Them Moving
items.summary: The article explains why urgent security patches often remain unimplemented. It highlights the need for observable proof that changes will not disrupt services, balancing security with availability. It calls for a structured approach to patch deployment.

items.title: British intelligence agency misplaced 'thousands' of storage devices, years later still can't say how many
items.summary: A British intelligence agency lost thousands of storage devices and remains uncertain of the exact count; the incident also involved an unchecked software bug linked to Terrorism Act detentions.

items.title: Polymarket confirms cyberattack on third-party provider after outages
items.summary: Polymarket experienced outages starting at 2 pm EST after a compromise of an unnamed third‑party provider; the downtime was caused by the provider’s breach.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Russian popular home goods chain faces days of disruption following cyberattack
items.summary: Poryadok, a Russian home‑goods chain with 48 stores, reported technical problems that made its website, mobile app and physical stores unavailable; the disruptions began on Sunday.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Binance Hit by Record-Breaking $6.3bn Hack in Largest Cryptocurrency Heist in History
items.summary: Binance suffered a $6.3 bn theft, the largest crypto heist recorded; analysts attribute the attack to a North Korean elite hacking unit.

items.title: Microsoft finally fixes VPN issues caused by September updates
items.summary: Microsoft resolved Always On VPN connection failures triggered by the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates, restoring VPN functionality.

items.title: Claude Code extension poisoned with persistent SSH backdoor
items.summary: Researchers found a tampered build of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension that installed a persistent SSH backdoor on developers’ machines; the malicious package was version 2.1.313 on Open VSX.

items.title: Drupal Commerce Core Vulnerability Exploited Against Online Stores
items.summary: Drupal reports a highly critical Commerce Core access bypass being exploited in the wild; store owners are urged to audit orders for potential compromise.

items.title: Hackers leak personnel data of 41,000+ Homeland Security staff, including ICE and border agents
items.summary: Hackers published personal data of over 41,000 U.S. Homeland Security staff, including ICE and CBP agents, exposing sensitive personnel information.

items.title: Drupal warns of critical Commerce Core flaw exploited in attacks
items.summary: Drupal has issued a patch advisory for a critical access bypass in its Commerce Core module. The flaw is actively exploited in the wild. Administrators should update immediately.

items.title: Filter generation in practice: from algorithms to LLMs
items.summary: Researchers automated security alert filter creation using an algorithm, a large language model, and a team of LLM agents. The approach streamlines threat detection.

items.title: $2 Million+ Drained From Polymarket Traders in New Supply Chain Attack
items.summary: A supply‑chain attack targeting Polymarket used malicious code in a website‑monitoring tool to hijack user sessions. Over $2 million was drained from traders.

items.title: Max-Severity GitLab Vulnerability Exploited Against Alpine Linux
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑97229 in GitLab allows unauthenticated attackers to run arbitrary code on Alpine Linux servers. The vulnerability was exploited in recent incidents.

items.title: Open-weight AI model GLM-5.3 cheated its way to correct answers
items.summary: Zhipu AI’s open‑weight model GLM‑5.3 was evaluated on 13 offensive cyber scenarios. It completed multiple multi‑stage attacks in the CyScenarioBench framework.

items.title: Binance links $6.3 billion crypto theft to compromised DevOps laptop
items.summary: Binance traced a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop. The incident highlights internal security risks.

items.title: Official Claude Code VS Code Extension Compromised to Install Persistent SSH Backdoor
items.summary: The official Anthropic Claude Code VS Code extension was compromised via the Open VSX registry, installing a persistent SSH backdoor. The breach was linked to the Cursor Marketplace.

items.title: TeamViewer Flaw Could Let Malicious Hosts Take Over Support Technicians’ Machines
items.summary: TeamViewer’s CVE‑2026‑111585 integer overflow flaw can enable malicious hosts to execute arbitrary code on the viewer’s machine. The vulnerability requires remediation.

items.title: $6 Billion Binance Hack Bears Hallmarks of North Korea’s TraderTraitor
items.summary: Blockchain analysis links Binance’s $6 billion theft to the North Korean TraderTraitor group. Binance is investigating a potentially compromised engineer laptop.

items.title: As Russia's Cyberwar Evolves, Belarus Steps Forward
items.summary: Belarusian APT “FrostyNeighbor” launched a destructive attack in Ukraine, raising concerns about deeper alignment with Russian cyber objectives.

items.title: Hackers Actively Exploit Highly Critical Drupal Commerce Core Authorization Bypass Flaw
items.summary: Drupal warns that threat actors are exploiting a critical authorization bypass in Commerce Core (CVE‑2026‑118539). The flaw affects versions 0.0.0‑2.41 and 3.0.0‑3.3.13. Users should apply the latest patch immediately.

items.title: CISA Adds Actively Exploited GitLab RCE and Cisco Firewall DoS Flaws to KEV
items.summary: CISA added two actively exploited vulnerabilities to its KEV list: GitLab RCE (CVE‑2026‑97229, CVSS 10.0) and a Cisco firewall DoS. Organizations should patch or mitigate these issues promptly.

items.title: Fake IT help desk callers got by on little more than names and email addresses
items.summary: Attackers posing as IT help desk staff used only names and email addresses to gain remote access, resulting in ransomware in some cases. Employees should verify caller identity before granting access.

items.title: What exactly is ISOC? And what does it mean for you?
items.summary: Gartner introduced the Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) category, reflecting a shift from traditional SIEM to more comprehensive security operations. ISOC emphasizes real‑time threat detection and response.

items.title: Scammers rebuild fake shopping sites within hours of a takedown
items.summary: Scammers rebuilt fake .shop domains within hours of takedown, sharing a single IP and identical HTML/JS to harvest payment data. Users should verify domain authenticity before purchasing.

items.title: Smart TVs can harbor unpatched security flaws and track what you watch
items.summary: Bitdefender’s 2026 IoT Security Landscape Report found smart TVs accounted for 22.7% of vulnerability observations, many unpatched flaws enabling tracking of viewing habits. Users should keep firmware updated.

items.title: In the year AI re-wrote the infosec rulebook, it’s comforting to know crypto exchanges still have bad security
items.summary: Binance froze $6.3 billion of assets after a security breach linked to an engineer’s compromised laptop. The incident highlighted ongoing security challenges for crypto exchanges.

items.title: Binance Suffers Security Breach Affecting $6.3 Billion in Assets, Nearly $3 Billion Frozen
items.summary: Binance reported a security incident that impacted approximately $6.3 billion in assets, with nearly $3 billion frozen on‑chain. The exchange is working to mitigate the breach.

items.title: Binance hit by record $6.3 billion crypto hack, scrambles to freeze funds
items.summary: Binance confirmed a $6.3 billion cyber heist, with investigators pointing to North Korean actors. The exchange is scrambling to freeze stolen funds.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Intigriti Bug Bytes #241 - October 2026 🚀
items.summary: Bug Bytes #241 (October 2026) showcases multiple high‑value exploits: a Microsoft Edge logic‑bug chain, a 1‑click RCE in Discord via Twitch embed, a $250K Chrome RCE bounty, a Cloudflare SVG sanitizer bypass, and a Google Flask session pickle RCE. The issue details several other findings.

items.title: OpenAI doubles ChatGPT Pro usage limits after backlash over planned 50% cut
items.summary: OpenAI reversed a planned 50% cut and doubled usage limits for ChatGPT Pro plans, maintaining separate limits for Dots usage. The change follows user backlash.

items.title: Researchers find bugs in 5 AI developer tools, with OpenAI and Microsoft flaws still unpatched
items.summary: Researchers discovered vulnerabilities in five AI development tools, including unpatched flaws in OpenAI and Microsoft products. The issues stem from embedded browser components.

items.title: Binance probes potential $5.8 billion crypto-theft hack
items.summary: Binance is investigating a possible security breach that could involve up to $5.8 billion in digital assets. The incident may become the largest cryptocurrency hack in history.

items.title: Hugging Face malware campaign returns to hijack GPUs for crypto mining
items.summary:
A crypto‑mining campaign using Hugging Face models returned after takedown, hijacking GPU servers and planting backdoors.
The malicious model was downloaded over 28,000 times.
A separate fake Solana starter kit on GitHub aims to trick AI coding agents into installing a NetSupport RAT.

items.title: Japan Airlines suffers third-party data breach exposing passenger info
items.summary:
Japan Airlines disclosed a data breach at Amadeus Passenger Service System that exposed personal data of approximately 92,000 customers.
The breach involved a third‑party service provider, Amadeus.

items.title: Polymarket halts trading after crypto-draining script breach, $2.5M traced
items.summary:
Polymarket temporarily suspended trading after hackers compromised a third‑party service to distribute a cryptocurrency‑draining JavaScript.
About $2.5 million in assets were traced to a suspected attacker wallet.

items.title: Anthropic-Themed Phishing Emails Bypass Top Security Tools
items.summary: Phishing emails themed around Anthropic bypassed several leading secure email gateway products despite containing multiple red flags.

items.title: Leaked DHS employee archive, Icepick, faces challenges to stay online
items.summary: The DHS employee archive 'Icepick' was removed by a contractor and blocked by a social media site, but later found a new hosting location.

items.title: Rethinking Cybersecurity Awareness in the AI Era
items.summary: The Reporters' Notebook series discusses trends from Cybersecurity Awareness Month, focusing on AI‑driven training and educating next‑generation workforces on modern risks.

items.title: Limited reports of PHP bug exploitation emerge
items.summary: Only a handful of PHP2Shell bug exploitations have been reported, with one campaign targeting U.S. government‑affiliated servers suspected to be Chinese.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Why CTF Competitions May Be More Important Than Ever
items.summary: Capture‑the‑flag contests help develop cybersecurity skills that are increasingly hard to acquire due to AI. They provide practical learning opportunities for early‑career professionals.

items.title: GM settles with 36 states for selling driver data, agrees to $220 million fine and reforms
items.summary:
General Motors agreed to pay $220 million to settle a lawsuit by 36 state attorneys general alleging unlawful sale of driver behavior data.
The company also agreed to implement data‑privacy reforms.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Fake crypto app on Apple App Store linked to $23K wallet theft
items.summary: A counterfeit cryptocurrency trading app, 'Padre Terminal', was removed from the Apple App Store and linked to theft of about $23,000 from 27 Solana wallets.

items.title: ThreatsDay: Critical Firewall Flaws, Banking Trojans Rented, Weaponized PDF, Token Theft + 26 More Stories
items.summary: ThreatsDay highlighted a range of attacks, including exposed firewall flaws, rented banking trojans, weaponized PDFs, and token theft, illustrating both sophisticated tactics and careless security gaps.

items.title: Suspected Chinese attackers built a custom PHP2Shell exploit and rooted 25 servers
items.summary:
Suspected Chinese threat actors used a custom PHP2Shell exploit to compromise 25 servers.
The attackers likely maintain access to a U.S. government-affiliated network.
No data exfiltration confirmed.

items.title: Hackers exploit Cisco SD-WAN flaw to deploy custom KeyDrift malware
items.summary:
APT group UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD‑WAN Controllers to deploy KeyDrift malware.
The flaw allows authentication bypass.
The attack demonstrates continued use of Cisco SD‑WAN vulnerabilities.

items.title: Claude Model Builds Exploits Across Major Browsers & OSes
items.summary:
Anthropic reports an unreleased Claude model discovered and chained vulnerabilities in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux.
The model identified multiple zero‑day exploits across major browsers and operating systems.
No public release of the findings yet.

items.title: Threat Brief: Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP: CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619 (Updated October 29)
items.summary:
CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 are critical PHP vulnerabilities affecting web servers and CMS platforms.
The flaws allow remote code execution and could compromise PHP installations worldwide.
Patching is recommended immediately.

items.title: A quiet week in infosec <.<
items.summary:
The Threat Source newsletter highlights PHP and Node.js as dominant topics in recent discussions.
It also notes ongoing community efforts to address security challenges.
No major incidents were reported this week.

items.title: BYOD cyberattack diverts ambulances and cancels classes at University of New Mexico health center
items.summary:
A ransomware attack on the University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center disrupted ambulance services, canceled surgeries, and forced medical students to leave classes.
The incident was caused by a BYOD-related breach.
The university is investigating the attack.

items.title: When Risk Becomes Personal: What Security Leaders Can Learn From a Cancer Diagnosis
items.summary:
The article discusses how risk management principles apply to personal health crises.
It highlights the importance of early detection, contingency planning, and decision-making under uncertainty.
The piece offers insights for security leaders.

items.title: Chinese hackers used VMware ESX zero-day; PHP2Shell and Fragnesia chained to root firewalls
items.summary:
Chinese threat actors exploited a VMware ESX zero‑day to conceal activity and chained PHP2Shell with the Fragnesia Linux kernel bug to compromise servers and firewalls.
Cisco confirmed a new firewall crash vulnerability.
The attack demonstrates multi‑stage exploitation.

items.title: Federal bankruptcy courts contractor says no data stolen during cyber intrusion
items.summary:
BAE Systems, a federal contractor, reported that no data was extracted during a cyber intrusion targeting its systems for federal bankruptcy courts.
The company is conducting a full investigation.
No breach of sensitive information was confirmed.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs caught hijacking searches
items.summary:
A search‑hijacking campaign involved 319 Chrome extensions with 13.4 million installs.
The extensions redirected users’ searches to tracking servers, generating revenue from Bing and Yahoo.
The campaign was discovered by security researchers.

items.title: Linux Kernel TCP Flaw With 9.8 CVSS Score Affects Ubuntu, Red Hat and Other Distributions
items.summary: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical TCP flaw in the Linux kernel, rated 9.8 CVSS. It affects Ubuntu, RHEL, and other distributions. Anthropic’s AI model produced an exploit that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute commands as root.

items.title: Threat Modeling With 4 Simple Questions on a White Board
items.summary: CISOs can use a four‑question whiteboard exercise to build effective threat models. The approach focuses on clarity and cost‑efficiency, avoiding large budgets.

items.title: Fake ChatGPT and Claude Apps Abuse Signed Executables to Deploy Crypto Miners
items.summary: Threat actors distribute malware disguised as AI desktop apps for Claude and ChatGPT. Fake GitHub projects deliver a loader that installs cryptocurrency miners under the Yoba campaign.

items.title: Google Touts Powerful Cybersecurity Capabilities in Gemini 4 Carbon Model
items.summary: Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon model achieved 88.2% on the SEC‑bench Pro test. The model is being rolled out to vetted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program.

items.title: How Secure Are US Elections? Voting Machine Risks and the Growing Threat of AI
items.summary: Unpatched voting machines, QR‑coded ballots, and AI‑driven influence campaigns expose vulnerabilities in US elections. The article highlights the need for stronger security measures.

items.title: NIK C2 Malware Can Use Victims’ OpenAI Keys for AI Queries
items.summary: NIK C2 malware can leverage victims’ OpenAI API keys to perform AI queries, enabling advanced malicious capabilities.

items.title: Yoba malware hides in fake desktop versions of ChatGPT and Claude
items.summary: The Yoba campaign uses fake GitHub repositories for apps like GPT‑5.6 Sol and Claude Opus to deliver a malware chain that culminates in a cryptocurrency miner.

items.title: Belgium's tax agency confirms cyberattack, pulls services offline
items.summary: Belgium’s tax authority experienced a cyberattack that forced it to take services offline and extend tax deadlines to November.

items.title: Microsoft fixes Remote Desktop failures caused by recent Windows updates
items.summary: Microsoft resolved an issue where non‑admin users could not connect via Remote Desktop when the Administrator protection feature was enabled after recent updates.

items.title: Cisco Open Sources Quarry to Catch AI Agent Attacks Hidden in Harmless Steps
items.summary: Cisco released Project Quarry, a rule language that detects AI agent attacks that emerge only across sequences of benign actions. The tool is open sourced for broader use.

items.title: Researchers broke the browsers built into VS Code, Cursor, Copilot, Codex and Claude Desktop
items.summary: Researchers bypassed built‑in browsers in five AI coding assistants, allowing local files or web pages to access the host system. The exploits enabled code execution, spoofed addresses, and full file system read.

items.title: 3 Ways AI Agents Already Operate in Your Browser
items.summary: AI agents can control authenticated browsers, interact with corporate apps, and access sensitive data while appearing as legitimate employees. Traditional security tools may struggle to differentiate their activity from human users.

items.title: CREST Urges Whole-Ecosystem Approach to Financial Cyber Resilience
items.summary: CREST released a framework advocating a whole‑ecosystem approach to strengthen cyber resilience across financial services.

items.title: IR trends Q3 2026: Actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks as ransomware activity increases
items.summary: Q3 2026 IR trends show increased ransomware activity; actors impersonate IT help desks in vishing attacks. Finance and public administration are top‑targeted industries.

items.title: CISA warns of Fragnesia Linux flaw chained in PHP2Shell attacks
items.summary: CISA warned federal agencies to patch a high‑severity Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw that is being chained with PHP2Shell attacks.

items.title: FTC to probe major companies over personalized pricing and pay
items.summary: FTC ordered nine major companies to provide detailed data on how they use personal data for individualized pricing and employee compensation.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Adobe, Veeam, Juniper Networks Patch Critical Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Adobe, Veeam, and Juniper Networks released patches for critical vulnerabilities that could lead to arbitrary code execution, authorization bypass, and privilege escalation.

items.title: Google's Gemini 4 Carbon Leads Benchmarks for Finding, Exploiting, and Patching Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, a model that leads benchmarks for finding, exploiting, and patching vulnerabilities, achieving high scores on SEC‑bench Pro and ExploitGym.

items.title: Volt Typhoon targeted enterprise control planes via ever-changing “Silent Train” relay network
items.summary: Volt Typhoon, a Chinese state‑sponsored APT, used a rotating relay network called Silent Train, built from compromised SOHO and IoT devices, to target enterprise control planes.

items.title: Cyberattack disrupts Belgian tax services before filing deadline
items.summary: A cyberattack disrupted Belgium’s MyMinfin tax platform before the filing deadline, prompting the Federal Public Service Finance to suspend access and investigate the breach.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.title: Shortlist of age checks for the UK's under-16 social media ban is out, 'some' adults will need verifying
items.summary: The UK government released a shortlist of age‑verification methods for the under‑16 social media ban. Some adults will be required to prove their age, while others may not.

items.title: Ubuntu Core Desktop returns as Canonical’s plan for an immutable default desktop
items.summary: Canonical has restarted development of Ubuntu Core Desktop, an immutable and attestable Ubuntu desktop that will become the default over time. The 2023 developer preview was considered insufficient. All components ship as snaps.

items.title: Windows 11 KB5127936 update released with 41 changes and fixes
items.summary: Microsoft released the KB5127936 preview cumulative update for Windows 11 25H2 and 26H2, containing 41 changes. Updates include improvements to File Explorer and the Cloud rebuild.

items.title: Attackers turn GitHub issues into supply chain campaign against 61 public repos in less than an hour
items.summary: Attackers leveraged GitHub issue workflows to launch a supply‑chain campaign against 61 public repositories in under an hour. The malicious workflow triggers automatically when a vulnerable action is detected.

items.title: Webinar: How to Build AI Threat Readiness Into Your Security Operations
items.summary: The webinar covers how to embed AI into security operations to shorten the time defenders have to respond. It highlights AI’s role in accelerating threat detection and response.

items.title: Telegram Android Flaw Lets Attackers Run Code When Users Answer Voice Calls
items.summary: A flaw in Telegram for Android allowed attackers to execute code on a victim’s phone when the user answered a voice call. The issue was fixed in version 12.10.4 released in late September.

items.title: The Rise of the Threat Operator: How AI Will Redefine Security Operations and Careers
items.summary: The report explains how AI is automating core SOC tasks such as alert investigation, evidence collection, and response actions. This shift is reshaping security operations roles and organization.

items.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
items.summary: Researcher Ben Zimmermann found 26,400 active cloud and AI credentials in 7.25 million public Gitee repositories. The exposed keys could be used by attackers to access services.

items.title: Online Scam Volumes Double to Overtake Phishing
items.summary: Akamai research indicates online scam detections exceeded six million in Q2 2026, doubling previous volumes and surpassing phishing incidents.

items.title: New Cisco firewall zero-day exploited to crash SSL VPN devices
items.summary: Cisco issued patches for a denial‑of‑service zero‑day in ASA and FTD software that attackers exploit to crash SSL VPN devices remotely.

items.title: Hackers Steal 2.6 Million Records From Sony’s Japanese ISP So-net
items.summary: Hackers exposed 2.6 million records from Sony’s Japanese ISP So‑net, including 54,401 email passwords and 16 bank account records.

items.title: Cisco Patches Actively Exploited ASA and FTD VPN Flaw That Can Crash Firewalls
items.summary: Cisco released patches for the high‑severity CVE‑2026‑76418 vulnerability in ASA and FTD software. The flaw, rated 8.6 on CVSS, could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to crash firewalls. Patches are now available.

items.title: ICO Reprimands Staffordshire Police After Domestic Abuse Breach
items.summary: The UK Information Commissioner’s Office reprimanded Staffordshire Police for a serious breach of personal data. The incident involved the mishandling of domestic abuse victim information. The regulator cited non‑compliance with privacy standards.

items.title: Cisco SD-WAN Zero-Day Exploitation Tied to Volt Typhoon’s ‘Silent Train’ Network
items.summary: Cisco Talos linked a key‑stealing SD‑WAN malware to infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon’s Silent Train network. The attack vector exploits Cisco SD‑WAN components. The analysis was published by SecurityWeek.

items.title: GitHub Launches npm Firewall to Block Malicious Packages Before Installation
items.summary: GitHub announced a preview of its npm firewall, designed to block malicious packages during installation. The firewall inspects metadata requests and downloads for malicious activity. It is currently available in public preview for npm only.

items.title: Shadowy AI Relay Disables OpenAI Codex, Claude Code Sandboxes
items.summary: A covert AI relay service supplies OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude code sandboxes to mainland China and other restricted regions. The service disables key security features, exposing users to risk. The relay operates without official authorization.

items.title: NIK C2: The new AI-enabled command-and-control framework
items.summary: Cisco Talos identified a new AI‑enabled command‑and‑control framework named NIK C2 circulating in the wild. The framework integrates machine learning for command execution. It represents an emerging threat vector.

items.title: Attackers Exploit Second Cisco Firewall VPN Zero-Day Since August
items.summary: An exploited flaw in Cisco’s Remote Access SSL VPN forces ASA and FTD firewalls to reload, enabling unauthenticated attackers to trigger a reboot. This is the second zero‑day discovered since August. The vulnerability is actively used in the wild.

items.title: NIST Publishes Guidance to Meet Federal Post-Quantum Deadlines
items.summary: NIST released guidance to help federal agencies prioritize post‑quantum cryptography adoption for sensitive systems. The guidance aims to meet the 2031 transition deadline. It outlines a phased implementation roadmap.

items.title: Attacker Tried to Exploit Alpine Linux’s GitLab via CVSS 10.0 Flaw Its Ruby Left Open
items.summary: An attacker attempted to exploit the critical GitLab CVE‑2026‑97229 vulnerability on Alpine Linux’s own GitLab server. The flaw, with a CVSS score of 10.0, could allow code execution via a crafted CI configuration. No successful exploitation was reported.

items.title: MR ROBOT Malware-as-a-Service Targets Indian Bank Customers
items.summary: MR ROBOT, an Android malware‑as‑a‑service platform, rents banking trojans that steal one‑time passwords and card data. The malware targets customers of Indian banks. It operates by compromising mobile devices.

items.title: Admin dropped the F-bomb in a password to show hackers who was really 1337
items.summary: Admin used profanity in a password to deter hackers, but overall security controls were inadequate.

items.title: HHS Filing Puts iRhythm Data Breach Toll at 8.2 Million
items.summary: iRhythm data breach exposed personal and device information; HHS estimates 8.2 million victims.

items.title: Hackers Exploited Cisco SD-WAN Flaw to Plant Malware Built to Steal Encryption Keys
items.summary: Attackers exploited a Cisco SD‑WAN flaw to deploy KeyDrift malware that copies encryption keys; the vulnerability was fixed in February.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Quietly Used Low-Severity ESXi Logging Flaw as Zero-Day
items.summary: CVE‑2026‑41709 allowed privileged attackers to perform actions without logging; Chinese threat actors used it as a zero‑day.

items.title: Unknown APT uses NetamLoader to attack a Win10 OS customized for governments in Asia
items.summary: Kaspersky identified a targeted campaign using NetamLoader against a government‑specific Windows 10 build in Asia.

items.title: Cyber Vulnerabilities Besiege Italy, Absent Clear Cause
items.summary: Researchers note that Italy’s cyber threat landscape differs markedly from global patterns, with unclear reasons.

items.title: Amatera: How the prolific infostealer works and spreads
items.summary: Amatera is a malware infostealer that topped ESET’s detections in Latin America in H1 2026. It demonstrates the professionalization of cybercrime through sophisticated distribution techniques.

items.title: Qualys CISO on what security teams can do as exploit campaigns grow
items.summary: Qualys CISO advises teams to focus on exposure windows, prioritize high‑risk flaws, and build trust amid rising AI‑discovered vulnerabilities.

items.title: China-Linked Hackers Exploited VMware ESX Zero-Day to Reduce Audit Trail Visibility
items.summary: CISA added CVE‑2026‑41709 to KEV after CrowdStrike confirmed China‑linked Warp Panda used it to hide activity in VMware ESX.

items.title: IT bosses are confident they’ve found the certificates they don’t know about
items.summary: Survey shows 40 % of senior IT leaders feel prepared for TLS renewals, but only 4 % have fully automated certificate management; 61 % experienced outages.

items.title: Attackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Internet-Exposed Palo Alto Networks Management Interfaces
items.summary: Palo Alto warned that threat actors are exploiting patched PHP2Shell vulnerabilities on publicly exposed management interfaces; active exploitation observed.

items.title: Shame and sleepless nights haunt scam victims long after the money is gone
items.summary: The 2026 ITRC Consumer Impact Report found that scam victims often suffer shame and self‑blame, while identity theft victims spend weeks repairing damage. The study surveyed 1,111 U.S. respondents.

items.title: Stolen staff logins are spreading attacks between K-12 school districts
items.summary: 808 K‑12 districts had staff credentials sold on dark‑web marketplaces, enabling attackers to move between schools. This represents 13% of the 6,116 MS‑ISAC members.

items.title: Officials seize domain of top bulletproof hosting provider Virtualine
items.summary: Authorities seized the domain of Virtualine, a Russian‑speaking bullet‑proof hosting provider that accounted for nearly 20% of illicit inflow tracked by researchers.

items.title: Smashing Security podcast #490: How Jared Kushner’s iPhone was allegedly hacked twice
items.summary: The Smashing Security podcast discussed claims that Jared Kushner’s iPhone was hacked twice by Dutch spies and Russian hackers, highlighting concerns about phone security. It also examined weak security keys used by trusted devices.

items.title: AI Takes Root in Hospital Corridors, Raises Security Stakes
items.summary: Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in healthcare, from intake forms to cancer screening. In some cases, the rapid deployment of AI outpaces cybersecurity controls, raising life‑and‑death risks.

items.title: Upwind Security Raises $400 Million at $3.8 Billion Valuation
items.summary: Upwind Security raised $400 million in a funding round, valuing the company at $3.8 billion. The round followed acquisition interest from firms such as Datadog.

items.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
items.summary: PHP2Shell shows attackers can exploit critical vulnerabilities before patches are applied, emphasizing that blast radius matters more than CVSS scores. Limiting access for service accounts, API keys, and AI agents is as important as patching.

items.title: Chrome and Firefox Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Chrome 156 fixed 52 bugs, while Firefox 159 released with 167 security patches, together addressing over 200 vulnerabilities.

items.title: How Rapid7 InsightGovCloud Supports BOD 22-01 Compliance
items.summary: Rapid7 InsightGovCloud supports BOD 22‑01 compliance by cataloguing exploited vulnerabilities and ensuring timely remediation for public and private sector organizations.

items.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
items.summary: FoxIO disclosed three TLS bugs in the GoAhead web server that allow revoked certificates or expose encrypted sessions, affecting hundreds of millions of devices.

items.title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
items.summary: Threat actors are probing the newly patched CVE‑2026‑101767, a critical RCE flaw in Oracle E‑Business Suite, after Oracle released a security patch last week.
